review_text:
I wanted to play Warframe, a fast paced parkour shooter. 

Then I encountered quest "The New War" which was slowest hours long slog-fest I've ever encountered, which I am locked inside.

Have hated every second of it, from the slowest most awkward ninja depicted in a video game (I include old NES games) to most shittiest sneak type missions of known galaxy. Every segment seemed to have different controls and mechanics, which you never had time to actually familiarize yourself with because they had nothing to do how rest of the game plays. Not a moment has been fun or engaging game play, which is achievement in itself.

Why e.g. a glaive is suddenly working totally differently how it had worked rest of the game up until now? No idea. Why are there supposed trails to the targets you have to find which are colored like background effects in that same area and do not seem to work half of the time anyway? No idea. Why everything is suddenly a slow paced walking simulator? No idea. Why guards have vision cones but they actually see WAY past those cones unlike any enemy before them (was e.g. hiding in a container but great that they see and shoot through walls). No idea. Why when you "die" it takes dozens of second to even replay? No idea. Why is every weapon suddenly preselected for you? No idea. Why when you fight the "owl" and most of the time you spend waiting to do damage while it regenerates and you cannot do any damage to it (= boss literally designed to waste your time)? No idea.

Who was that uniquely intelligent person who came up ALL that? No idea. Was it the same person who thought it was that such "brilliant" idea to lock new players within Duviri Paradox with no way out, if they happened to make the mistake of choosing Duviri start instead of Warframe? (Because they are new players and have no idea how the game is supposed to work, or what Duviri even is if they do not do homework before playing).

It's been as curios as has been base design ideas behind e.g. Total War Warhammers as example. What people have most liked about Total Wars? Sandbox style gameplay - make your own decisions how to proceed. So what should main campaigns be like? Everything BUT sandbox, constant ticking timers and forcing player to do stuff within limited time-frame. What people like in Warframe? fast paced movement and shootouts with customizable frames and weapons which suit your personal playstyle. So what should hours long main quest be like? Everything BUT previously mentioned elements. That is a very curious design philosophy behind game design, make your games less fun to play.

Here's a free to read negative review, no need for platinum.
reason: Criticises quest design; uses spend about time waiting, not money

I was banned for using a "cheating software" (why the hell would I cheat, with so much time and money in the game). I can assure you, I wasn't cheating. While my ban is lifted, this is the second time this month that something on my pc tripped their anti cheating software. So I'm now just too afraid to touch the game, because they're calling me a cheater, and refuse to provide any further details, or help on what might be tripping the program so I can remove it, instead calling me a cheater and telling me to stop trying to modify the program when I go to support.
I know that I'm some random dude on the internet, but why the hell would I cheat on this game. I have no reason to, I've done most of my farming already and just play for events / to get MR. 
As for what I THINK is the issue, a warning to anyone: Don't run Stable Diffusion while playing, instead of warning you that something is "modifying your memory" (what the fuck does that mean) they silently ban you a week later.
